figures.caption: Table 1: Full-context Top-1 retrieval accuracy (%) across six representations. Mean SE denotes the average gain (pp) over independent retrieval.

Figure 3: Context-marginalized retrieval performance and context robustness on BLUR across query-context sizes m. (a) Context-marginalized Top-1 retrieval accuracy (CM-Top1); shaded bands indicate standard deviation across subjects. (b) Same-query Context Consistency (CC)
Table 3: Average same-query context consistency (CC,%) across reduced query contexts. Final column reports the average across the six frozen representations.

Figure 4: Joint profiles of structural exploitability and context robustness. (a) Mean reducedcontext Top-1 SE versus mean Context Consistency (CC), across six frozen representations and four reduced context sizes. (b) Context-size-specific SE and CC, averaged across representations and standardized across rules within each metric and context size.

Table 4: Validation on THINGS-MEG. Full-context Top-1 is averaged across four held-out subjects. Reduced-context results are averaged over m ∈ {25, 50, 100, 150}. SE denotes Top-1 structural exploitability relative to independent retrieval.
Figure 5: CM-Top1 and CC across query-context sizes for BLUR (a,b) and UBP (c,d).
Table 6: Relationship between partition rounds and per-query context counts in CMRE.

Figure 6: Origin of full-context Top-1 structural gains. For each inference method, the diverging bars show the average numbers of wrong-to-correct (W→C; blue) and correct-to-wrong (C→W; orange) transitions relative to independent retrieval. The flows show the ground-truth (GT) rank under independent retrieval for W→C queries. Results are averaged across six representations and ten LOSO folds.

Table 7: Full-context Top-5 retrieval accuracy (%) across six representations. Mean SE denotes the average gain (pp) over independent retrieval. Top-5 is not reported for Hungarian because hard one-to-one assignment produces a single discrete assignment rather than a ranked candidate list.

Table 9: Statistical significance of reduced-context CM-Top1 gains over independent retrieval. Each comparison uses the ten held-out subjects as independent observations after averaging over six representations and four reduced query context sizes. Reported p-values are Holm-adjusted across the six inference methods.
Table 10: CM-Top5 structural exploitability (SE, pp), averaged over the reduced query-context sizes.

Figure 7: Decomposition of same-query Context Consistency. Queries are categorized as Stable Correct, Stable Wrong, or Context-Sensitive according to their CM-Top1 predictions across sampled query contexts. (a) Average proportions of the three categories across m. (b) Stable-Correct and Context-Sensitive proportions at each context size. (c) Average CC versus Stable-Correct rate, where color denotes the representation, marker shape denotes the inference method, and bubble size represents the Stable-Wrong rate.

Figure 8: CMRE convergence over context-construction rounds on BLUR. Absolute deviations of (a) CM-Top1 and (b) Context Consistency (CC) from the T = 50 reference as the number of partition rounds increases. Curves correspond to CSLS, Sinkhorn, and Hungarian and are averaged across context sizes. The dashed line marks the T = 10 setting used in the main experiments. Both metrics are already close to the high-budget reference at T = 10.

Table 12: Comparison of the original CMRE protocol and independently sampled contexts on BLUR. Each entry reports reference → independent-sampling results (%). Independent sampling uses ten contexts per query and ten seeds. At m = 150, the reference for the three stable-prediction categories uses a matched budget of ten evaluations per query.
Table 13: Joint effects of query-context size m and gallery size Ng on BLUR. Top-1 accuracy (%) is reported with SE (pp) as a subscript. bold indicates the best rule.
Table 14: Joint effects of query-context size m and gallery size Ng on UBP. Top-1 accuracy (%) is reported with SE (pp) as a subscript. bold indicates the best rule.

Figure 9: Robustness to gallery expansion on BLUR. (a) Top-1 retrieval accuracy as the gallery size increases from Ng = 200 to Ng = 2000 while keeping all 200 EEG queries fixed. (b) Corresponding Top-1 gain over independent retrieval.
